title: Huffman coding
summary: Optimal prefix code: assign shorter codes to more frequent symbols. Algorithm: build a binary tree by repeatedly merging the two least frequent nodes. The code for each symbol is the path from root to leaf (0=left, 1=right). Huffman codes are optimal (minimum expected length) among prefix codes. Average length ≤ H(X) + 1.

structure.meaning: Priority queue of symbols by frequency. Repeatedly extract two min, merge, insert back. Continue until one node.
Traverse tree from root. Left edge = 0, right edge = 1. Code = path bits.
L = Σ p(x) * len(code(x)). H(X) ≤ L < H(X) + 1.
Sort codes by length, then assign lexicographically. Enables efficient decoding with a lookup table.
Update tree dynamically as symbols are processed. No need to transmit the tree.

notes: Huffman coding is used in JPEG, MP3, DEFLATE, and many other formats.
Arithmetic coding achieves closer to H(X) (no +1 overhead) but is slower.
Huffman codes are prefix-free: no code is a prefix of another. Enables unambiguous decoding.
Canonical Huffman codes can be decoded with a single lookup table.
Adaptive Huffman (FGK, Vitter) updates the tree on the fly.
